rule.description: Report every fragment that resolves one of the inheritable toast presentation options (icon, invert, richColors, unstyled/styled, closeButton, closeButtonAriaLabel, duration, className/classNames, descriptionClassName, cancelButtonStyle, actionButtonStyle) against a second source - a second read of the option, a bare identifier naming the value from another layer, or a helper call that hands the option value and its fallback to the call site. Fragments are only meaningful together: the smell is the number of distinct modules that keep such local copies of the same inheritance contract.

checks.description: The toast rendering component re-states, per option, that its own toast value wins over the value the toaster wired in.
checks.detected_relation: toast record option -> toaster-level default of the same option
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: This relation is the render-time half of the inheritance contract; each re-statement is a local copy of a rule that belongs to the contract, and the same copy exists independently in other modules (wiring, store, assets, skin helpers). Changing the precedence for one option means hunting every copy.

matches.evidence: Remaining-time ref seeded with `toast.duration || durationFromToaster` (the plain default constant continues the chain), inside the toast component, line 103.
Close-button visibility memo computes `toast.closeButton ?? closeButtonFromToaster` because unset on the toast must fall back to the toaster, line 120.
Duration re-computation memo repeats the expiry precedence `toast.duration || durationFromToaster` a second time inside the same component, line 124.
Cancel-button inline style picks `toast.cancelButtonStyle || cancelButtonStyle`, i.e. the toast's style over the toaster-level configuration, line 484.
Action-button inline style picks `toast.actionButtonStyle || actionButtonStyle`, the same relation for the action button, line 503.

checks.description: The module declaring the option types keeps its own layering helper: per-toaster toastOptions values beat the <Toaster> component's own props.
checks.detected_relation: per-toaster toastOptions option -> <Toaster> prop of the same option
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: This is the wiring half of the same contract, kept in a different module than the render half; the precedence for duration and closeButton exists both here and at the per-toast sites.

matches.evidence: Wiring helper layers `toastOptions?.duration ?? duration` below the option interface, line 127.
Same layering for the close button: `toastOptions?.closeButton ?? closeButton`, line 128.

checks.description: The store keeps its own precedence list: which stored presentation fields carry over when a toast update does not restate them.
checks.detected_relation: update payload option -> stored record option of the same toast
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: This relation decides field-by-field which layer survives an in-place update, in a store-local restatement of the same option inheritance; a precedence change for one option (or a new carried field) must be edited here and wherever else the option's precedence lives.

matches.evidence: `update.icon !== undefined ? update.icon : stored.icon`, an identity ternary because an explicit `null` icon must win over the stored one, line 40.

checks.description: The extracted skin resolvers re-state, one option at a time in their own module, that the toast's value beats the toaster-level value.
checks.detected_relation: toast record skin option -> toaster-level skin option
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: These resolvers hold the identical concept of inheritance as the render sites they replaced and the wiring helper, but in yet another module of their own.

matches.evidence: `toast.jsx || toast.unstyled || toasterUnstyled`, the styled/opt-out chain, line 23.

checks.description: The icon chain keeps its precedence in the asset module: a toast-provided icon beats the per-type icon configured on the toaster, with the built-in asset behind them.
checks.detected_relation: toast record icon -> configured icon set for the toast's type (-> built-in asset)
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: One more module owns precedence for one presentation option of the same contract; an icon-precedence change (for example letting a configured icon of an explicit `null` toast icon through) is made here while every other option lives elsewhere.

matches.evidence: `toast.icon || icons?.[toastType]` heading the chain that falls through to `getAsset(toastType)`, line 28.

excluded: Class-name and stylesheet concatenations (cn(classNames?.closeButton, toast?.classNames?.closeButton) and siblings): ordered listings of class reads from every layer, not a precedence pick between two sources of one option; the rule counts precedence decisions, never concatenations.

Presence and negation checks (toast.dismissible !== false in the component, data.dismissible === undefined ? true : data.dismissible in the store): they compare against a constant, so no second layer of the option exists at the site.
Display string defaults (toast.className || '', toast.descriptionClassName || ''): the fallback is a literal with no layer to name.

Single-layer reads passed per toaster (toastOptions?.className, toastOptions?.style, toastOptions?.closeButtonAriaLabel and the wiredToastOptions plumbing around them): nothing is resolved against a second source at these sites.

Memo dependency arrays next to the close-button and duration sites: they restate the inputs the effect depends on; the precedence decision next to them is reported once at its own expression, not twice.

Resolver calls that receive whole layer inputs (a record, a configured set, a fallback value object) instead of the option value plus its fallback: the precedence decision is inside one shared owner's body rather than at the call site, which is the intended shape and lives with the other fragments of that owner.
src/hooks.tsx (useIsDocumentHidden) and the layout/geometry constants: lifecycle and geometry, no inheritable-option decision exists there.
